method: Independent source/definition review and independently written exhaustive finite DAG path enumeration. No Lean compilation, proof edits, or theorem-refutation claim.

findings.location: Section 2.2, printed p.5 (PDF p.7), continuation p.6 (PDF p.8); content/greg.tex lines55-73
findings.claim: Potential sums distances above beta/2, denominator p counts pairs above beta, then some hopdistance >= phi/p.
findings.verdict: False literal intermediate inequality, with unbounded multiplicative error.
findings.family: Unit-weight directed path 0->1->...->(2k+2), H empty, k>=1, n=2k+3, beta=2k.

calculation.example_k2: n=7, beta=4, phi=40, p=3, maxhop=6, phi/p=40/3>6

findings.repair_limits: Use q=count of distances>beta/2 for averaging. To preserve subsequent use of a distance>beta, select a maximum-hopdistance pair (the algorithm is not halted), which also exceeds phi/q. This supports a repaired constant-factor potential-reduction argument, with ordinary rounding for small beta. It does not itself prove the subsequent claim of Omega(beta^2) eliminated pairs per greedy round or the log-free bound. The same family has p=3, so an unconditional per-round Omega(beta^2) reduction in the original p is impossible without exceptions or a different measure. Section2.1 gives a separate warmup analysis and is not refuted by this diagnostic.
findings.scope: A recap/proof-step error; no counterexample to the paper main results or to the underlying Berman-Raskhodnikova-Ruan theorem.

findings.verdict: False under the exact source-relative earliest-chain-entry definition, including for a globally longest normalized-shortest path and subpath endpoint pairs in S.

example.cover_checks: 9 disjoint chains cover all10 vertices; 9^3=729<=8*10^2, hence9<=2*10^(2/3); uncovered count0. Chain7->8 already exists, so supershortcutting adds no missing edge.
example.splicing_failure: Earliest node reachable from0 on chain[7,8] is7; earliest from1 is8. Alternative is valid from1 but its concatenation with prefix0->1 is invalid from0.

findings.repair_limits: Validity itself can be hereditary; optimality fails because admissibility depends on the starting vertex and valid alternatives need not be spliceable. The proof needs a different progress argument or a modified compositional distance/validity notion. Merely invoking ordinary shortest-path optimal substructure is insufficient. This example does not disprove the cubic potential-reduction conclusion, Lemma5.7, or Theorem5.1; it disproves the cited step supporting them.
